Definition: something intwined, i.e. a string, wreath or foliage
BiblicalUsage: This word names something twisted or interlaced — wreathen chains of pure gold on the high priest’s breastplate, fastened to the ephod, and the ‘wreaths of chain work’ on the capitals of Solomon’s pillars. It is the work of the craftsman, gold and bronze twisted into ornament.
TheologicalSignificance: It is a craftsman’s word, and it carries no doctrine of its own — though I notice where the wreathen work goes: on the breastplate over the priest’s heart and on the pillars of the house, beauty set where God is worshipped.
